title: About
text:
PULSE has been specifically designed to connect early-career researchers with opportunities and skills that support long-term career sustainability across sectors. To meet this goal, the PULSE training program has been developed using the European Competency Framework for Researchers (ResearchComp). As such, being or hosting a PULSE postdoc has specific requirements that differ from some traditional postdoctoral training programs.
The PULSE Training website hosts training modules developed for the PULSE postdocs. For more information on the program, visit the SciLifeLab PULSE Page

title: TST Webinar Schedule
text:
Format
Before the call:

A video (approximately 30 minutes) of expert-led content will be provided along with any suggested materials or reflective questions.

During the call:

The cohort will split into discussion groups, and discussion will be led by an assigned postdoc moderator.

After the call:

After the discussion, the postdoc moderators will collaboratively generate a short news piece (maximum 1000 words) representing the Future Leaders’ Perspective.
The PULSE communications team will help in publishing this piece on SciLifeLab channels. If the piece is of particular interest and suitability, it may also be submitted to journals or news markets.

The format of these discussions is designed to build skills in negotiation, moderation, collaboration, critical thinking, and public communication.
The moderator role will rotate with each discussion and each postdoc is expected to contribute to moderation and writing once per year.

title: Annual Workshop Overview
text:

The four transferrable skills sessions of the annual meeting will be:

The meeting will also include research presentations and scientific discussion to support interactions between group leaders, postdocs, and others.

title: Resources
text:
Building Scientific Influence
Building a public-facing presence with influence can take time. If social media is a tool you are interested in to make contacts at conferences, communicate your research highlights, or follow scientific leaders, we suggest creating a Bluesky account1 and/or LinkedIn account.
Don’t forget to follow SciLifeLab!    .

title: Resources
text:
Collaborate and Share
We have set up a Zotero library for PULSE postdocs to collect citations during the Transferrable Skills Training Program. All citations used in the training material can be found in this library.
We have added a few references and interesting articles on career assessment, ECR in Sweden, and the culture of science. Request an invitation to add articles you have found interesting for career development and leadership.
